narrative.overview:
DBBL built the country's digital rails (the first ATM network, the first mobile bank, NexusPay), and the system is the visual voice of a bank that does not need to shout, now turned up for Gen Z. It plays the consumer-bank category standard straight, at Revolut and Monzo craft: deep indigo is the base (the hero, Loans, Media, the NexusPay story and every dark band), and full-colour section fields carry the energy, one per section, each with a job. Lime is the Students field and the offers ticker, Rocket magenta is the Rocket field, DBBL green is the CSR field and the Fast Track and ATM accent, red is the live campaign. Sun yellow is the sticker colour and never a ground. Paper and white sections sit between the fields so the colour reads as rhythm, not noise. Persuasion comes from real proof and live campaigns (counted numbers, a dated set of firsts, the UDYOG feature, real offer terms) set in big, tight Bricolage Grotesque.

Density is generous: sections breathe at 96 to 128px of vertical padding inside a 1360px container, headlines are left-aligned and large, and each section has one job. Rounding scales with the object: 16px for interface surfaces, 24px for tickets and stickers, 28 to 32px for the big colour tiles and the campaign feature. Shadows stay ambient and indigo-tinted. Photography is full-bleed and graded with indigo or green, never a grey scrim. Motion has two registers: calm and expensive for structure (long ease-out-expo curves, 24px rises, pinned scroll stories), and springy for the Gen Z layer (stickers that pop in tilted, tickets you can drag, a ticker that never stops, a dial pad that types itself). All of it turns off under reduced motion.

The system rejects the cluttered link-farm bank portal (the mega menu holds the depth so the page does not have to) and the novelty-world gimmick alike. It is bilingual by construction: every display and text stack falls back to Anek Bangla, and Bangla mode loosens line height and drops negative tracking.
keyCharacteristics: Indigo base with one full-colour field per section, each colour owning a job: lime (students, offers), magenta (Rocket), green (CSR, Fast Track, ATMs), red (live campaigns), sun (stickers only).
Lime is still the primary action on every dark ground.
Bricolage Grotesque display set tight (-0.03 to -0.05em) and big; Hanken Grotesk text at 17px.
Pill buttons with a circular arrow chip whose arrow slides through on hover.
Radius scales with size: 16px surfaces, 24px tickets and stickers, 28 to 32px colour tiles and features.
Sticker badges, ticket-shaped offer cards, colour tiles with oversized numerals.
Two signature scroll moments: the indigo circle spreading from the NexusPay phone, and the tilted card frame opening to full-screen video.
Bilingual (English and Bangla) with Anek Bangla as a first-class fallback in every stack.

rules.name: The One Field Per Section Rule
rules.body: Each section takes one ground: indigo-950, paper, white, or one full-colour field (lime for Students, rocket for Rocket, green-700 for CSR). Colour tiles and stickers inside a section may mix the palette; the ground does not.

rules.name: The Colour Has A Job Rule
rules.body: Lime means students, offers and the action on dark; magenta means Rocket; green means growth, safety, Fast Track, ATMs and CSR; red means a live campaign or an alert; sun means a sticker or accent. Inside a multi-colour set (offer tickets, stickers, firsts) the colours rotate freely, but no colour becomes a section ground outside its job.

rules.name: The Sun Never Grounds Rule
rules.body: Sun fills stickers, badges, tiles and icon chips, and colours an accent word on magenta. It is never a section background.

rules.name: The Citrus On Dark Rule
rules.body: On indigo, magenta, green or a photograph, the primary action is lime (or white on a colour field). On paper or white the primary action is indigo-600 (green-600 in the Fast Track section), never a lime button or lime text. On the lime Students field the action is indigo-950.

rules.name: The Tinted Scrim Rule
rules.body: Photographs are graded with indigo-950 or green-700-family gradients that run from the text side outward. Never a neutral grey or black scrim.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Display type is always semibold or bold with negative tracking between -0.015em (small titles) and -0.06em (the campaign numeral); line height never exceeds 1.04 on headlines.

rules.name: The Bangla Breathing Rule
rules.body: In Bangla mode the whole page switches to Anek Bangla, body line height rises to 1.7, display line height to 1.12 and display tracking resets to 0. Never apply Latin negative tracking to Bangla script.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every number that represents money, a count, a phone number, a USSD code or a card number uses tabular lining figures.

rules.name: The Overlap Rule
rules.body: Exactly one element bridges the hero and the page: the white quick-action dock, pulled up 64px on the float shadow.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Hover Rule
rules.body: Cards and tickets rest at Card and move to Lift on hover; nothing gains a shadow it did not need to separate from its ground.

dos: Do keep indigo as the base: indigo-950 for dark bands and photo grades, indigo-600 for the primary action on light grounds.
Do give each section one ground, and give each full-colour field its job: lime for Students and the offers ticker, rocket for Rocket, green-700 for CSR, red-600 for the live campaign card.
Do use lime (#c8f169) as the primary action on every dark or colour ground.
Do use sun (#ffcf3d) for stickers, badges, tiles and accents only.
Do scale radius with the object: 16px surfaces, 24px tickets and stickers, 28 to 32px colour tiles and features, full pills for controls.
Do let stickers and tickets tilt and spring, and straighten them on hover.
Do grade every photograph with an indigo-950 or green gradient from the text side.
Do set headlines in Bricolage Grotesque 600 with negative tracking and line height at or below 1.04.
Do set every money, count, phone, code and card number in tabular lining figures.
Do rest cards on the Card shadow and move them to Lift on hover.
Do turn off every loop, spring, drag, pin and parallax under reduced motion, leaving the final state in place.
Do keep every stack falling back to Anek Bangla and switch to the Bangla rhythm (1.7 body, 1.12 display, 0 tracking) in Bangla mode.
donts: Don't use sun as a section ground.
Don't use rocket magenta as a section ground outside the Rocket section, or red outside live campaigns, alerts and the offer set.
Don't put two full-colour fields in one section, or place two field sections back to back without the colour having a job.
Don't put lime text or lime buttons on paper or white grounds.
Don't use grey or black scrims over photography.
Don't use hard offset shadows or visible card borders; separate with ground and ambient shadow.
Don't add uppercase tracked eyebrows or kickers above headlines; the headline leads.
Don't apply negative Latin tracking to Bangla text.
Don't turn the homepage into a link farm; depth belongs in the mega menu and footer.
placeholders: Logo mark (web/src/components/Logo.tsx) is a concept stand-in; replace with DBBL's official logo SVG.
Hero, CSR and other lifestyle photography is Unsplash stand-in imagery for DBBL's own shoots; the Fast Track photo, TV-ad posters and billboards are DBBL's own published assets.
Phone screens, the dial pad, the Rocket notification, the sample card number and amounts are illustrative synthetic demo data.
